content.comment_body: Hello, Yesterday, I programmed my [product_name] without any issues. Today, it is prompting me for a password, but I never set one. The device now shows three menus, which seems to indicate it is not in administrator mode. When trying to switch to ADMIN, it requires a password. I’ve already tried common passwords like "LOGO", "logo", "ADMIN", and "admin" without success. I am certain I didn’t set a password yesterday, so I’m confused. Is there a way to reset the device or regain access? Please advise. Best regards, [user_name]

A factory reset is not possible with [article_no].Standard (FS: 02). This function is only available from [product_name] 8.FS4 (FS: 04) and onward. If your [product_name] is operating in operator mode, the menu will display "Switch to ADMIN". The standard password should be "LOGO". Can you clarify which process is prompting for the password?

Thanks for your response. The controller asks for a password because it has switched to operation mode. I was able to clear the program from the device, but still can’t access admin mode, as the password "LOGO" isn’t working. I have never changed this password. Is there any other way to revert to admin mode or reset the device? I haven’t experienced this issue before.
As mentioned earlier, a factory reset is only available from FS: 04 and later versions. If I were you, I’d contact support for assistance.

To conclude the discussion: Support was very helpful. It turns out you can change the password by clearing both the program and password while connected to the device. Then, under "Access control settings," you can update the password through the "Control operation from [product_name] TD" function. This option also changes the device password. After doing this, you can switch from OP mode to ADMIN mode. Thanks!

Happy to hear you resolved it. One thing still confuses me: you mentioned not changing the password, yet the default "LOGO" was not accepted. This suggests the password may have been altered unknowingly.

Yes, I confirmed I didn’t change the password, and support couldn’t explain how it happened. I’m sure I didn’t modify it at all between two days ago and yesterday. The only notable difference is that I used [product_name] V8.0 two days ago and [product_name] V8.1.1 yesterday.

analysis.insight_summary: A user unexpectedly lost admin access to their [product_name] device when prompted for a password they never set, even after trying defaults. Attempts to switch modes or reset failed because factory reset is supported only on updated versions. Ultimately, support provided a solution, indicating password and access issues might be linked to software version changes and device access controls, but there’s no straightforward process for restoring default access.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to maintain admin access on their device whenever no password was set, and wants a reliable method to regain access or restore default settings if locked out.
